title: How to debug Unity using AI?
author: AgenticGameDev
selftext:
Any one using AI to debug Unity code? Like breakpoints, stacktrace, variables and such..

If so how and what tools?

I was thinking about making something. But no point if good things exist out there. Did not find any one when I looked.

comments.author: RyiahTelenna
comments.body:
>Any one using AI to debug Unity code?

I just pass the entire script along with error messages.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
Ai doesnt need those to debug code... you literally just describe the issue in your prompt and that's it. You actually dont even have to point it to the right file. As long as it has visibility to your project folder. It will just troubleshoot

Obviously its faster and better if you already narrow it down and you can just tell it to fix this class or that method

If Ai is failing to fix the issue, then you have to resort to using another AI or fix it yourself 

Sometimes I get lazy and I just copy-paste any error messages I see back to AI and it works that way too

replies.author: AgenticGameDev
replies.body: Interesting. My experience is that it struggles when we cross layers like c# to components which reference some other components. Sure basic jump mechanics works but any thing advanced and it some times get spinning but no result especially if it’s spatial.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
If it is spatial, you should provide screenshots for AI to analyze. I usually go around the builder at that point, put my higher AI model in thinking mode and send it the screenshot

It is not really about advanced mechanics. You just have to keep in mind that AIs dont approach the project like we do. Its still a machine so you have to convert the issue into a "digestable" format if that makes sense

replies.author: AgenticGameDev
replies.body: Agree 100% that is why I’m investing if I’m alone thinking about AI debugging using breakpoints as a last resort. Got all up to this point it feels like but not that breakpoint debugging.

replies.author: mikecrash
replies.body: It sucks for me too man, and I’m using the unity MCP and every tool I can find and it still take a long time to fix. Tests, sub-claude docs, working on one thing at a time help, but it’s a slow process

replies.author: AgenticGameDev
replies.body: So what tools more than unity mcp?

replies.author: mikecrash
replies.body: So, ask claude code directly about tools to use related to unity soecifically, plugins/resoure packs from the store/ etc that can help it work faster/better

replies.author: AgenticGameDev
replies.body: I have done that and got nothing fore breakpoint debugging. :)

comments.author: BertJohn
comments.body:
Chances are what your trying to debug is lacking a foundational API that's required or you are missing a skill/tool in your AI Agent that can properly do the tasks you require of it, And not an issue of the AI itself's produced code. 

  
For example, Unity MCP bridging Codex into the editor, If you try to have it create complex curves in a simulation on a dimensional grid based off scale of an object, It won't know how to calculate the curves properly. This isn't Codex's fault but more of the user's for not introducing a foundation like Splines or helper API functions that set a concrete core for the AI to create the proper curvature you are looking in a dynamic environment.

replies.author: AgenticGameDev
replies.body: I agree! This is important. I normally spend about 1-4h planning to weed out all architecture and API and what exist things before a new implementation. But after all that is done I some times end up with hard bugs that I need to debug manually to solve. Not a problem But trying to figure out a way so I don't have to....

comments.author: AnarchyDex
comments.body:
yeah the spatial cross-layer stuff is where most setups fall apart imo. the issue isn't really the model, it's that most tools are working off static context  file contents, maybe a hierarchy dump without ever seeing actual runtime state.

i've been hacking on this with Movesia (full disclosure, i'm building it) basically a desktop app that holds a live connection to the editor so the agent can read console output, check actual component values, and verify whether what it intended actually happened. right now that's read-only at runtime, but play-mode integration where it can run the game, watch what happens, and iterate is what i'm working on next. won't magically fix spatial reasoning (that's more of a model problem) but it does close the loop on "did my change actually work."

if you're scoping this space yourself, lmk interesting problems either way.

replies.author: AgenticGameDev
replies.body: I'm about to release a test tool. To simplify testing in Unity. Where step debugging would be a nice addition to the rest.
